candidate.derivedAnswer: One real pair and two nonreal complex pairs, choice E
candidate.answerReason: An equivalent substitution gives \(t^3=1\), with one real root and two distinct nonreal roots. Each determines exactly one solution pair. The historical word 'imaginary' means nonreal complex here.

methods.label: Substitute the repeated expression
methods.explanation:
Both equations contain \(x+1\), since \(xy+y=(x+1)y\). Set \(t=x+1\). The system becomes
\[
y=t^2,\qquad ty=1,
\]
so substitution gives \(t^3=1\). Conversely, every such \(t\) gives a solution through \(x=t-1\) and \(y=t^2\).

Factor the difference of cubes:
\[
t^3-1=(t-1)(t^2+t+1)=0.
\]
The first factor gives \(t=1\), hence the real pair \((x,y)=(0,1)\). For the quadratic factor, completing the square gives
\[
\left(t+\frac12\right)^2=-\frac34,
\qquad t=\frac{-1\pm i\sqrt3}{2},
\]
where \(i^2=-1\). For these roots, \(t^2=-t-1\), so the other two pairs are
\[
\left(\frac{-3+i\sqrt3}{2},\frac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2}\right)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\left(\frac{-3-i\sqrt3}{2},\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]
They are distinct nonreal pairs. The factorization includes every possible \(t\), and distinct values of \(t\) give distinct values of \(x\), so no pairs are omitted or counted twice. In the historical choices, 'imaginary' means nonreal complex. There is therefore one real pair and two imaginary pairs, choice E.
